lead: Digital World Acquisition / DWAC — Truth Social's launch is set for a holiday
smaller: Bitcoin / BTC-USD — the dip-buyers meet Buterin's winter
Tesla / TSLA — Musk picks a fight with the SEC
Gold Miners ETF / GDX — the war hedge waits for Tuesday
why_lead: Truth Social's App Store release was a dated pending catalyst for Monday 21 February, a US market holiday (Reuters n0932, Axios n1766, Slate n1763, after Reuters' tester report n1742); the launch itself had not happened at the cutoff and is written only as scheduled. Attention evidence is mainstream coverage (Guardian beta glimpse n1752, Vanity Fair n1744, Snopes rumour check n1755). DWAC closed at 84.32 USD on 18 February, +15.32% over 20 sessions and +2.83% over five (-1.37% on the day) against a falling Nasdaq 100 (-1.14%) and Robinhood (-11.34% 5s). Nunes's end-of-March full-operation timetable (n1765) supplies the break; the Virgin Galactic round trip (n0523 surge, CNBC n0844 and Forbes n0903 on Palihapitiya's board exit, SPCE 5s -0.47%) is the analog; the Smart Money split is NYT's crowded field (n1767) vs the Parler/Gettr CEOs (n1730), with Bloomberg's S&P crash hedge (n2043) and Wolf Street's leverage warning (n1310). Relation to strictly earlier retail notes (1-18 February): DWAC was a 17 February smaller item ('Truth Social's first screenshot'), built on the Forbes screenshot, Newsweek, Bloomberg Parler/Gettr and Time headlines. The repeat lead is justified by newly published evidence (the 20 February Reuters/Axios/Slate launch-date reports, Nunes's timetable, the tester and beta reports) and a new angle (a dated catalyst landing on a closed market and the holiday gap); of the 17 February headlines only Bloomberg's Parler/Gettr item and none of the screenshot/Newsweek/Time items remain. Virgin Galactic was a 16 February smaller item and is used only as an analog updated with the 18 February board exit and round-tripped price.
why_smaller: Bitcoin: material update with a new angle. The weekend's only open market fell 4.21% on 20 February and 13.78% over five sessions (Ether -17.33% 5s), with the 20-session change at -0.13%, as Buterin welcomed another winter (Bloomberg n1001, 19 February) and Business Insider Africa cast Bukele as the meme-stock generation's dip-buying president (n1762, 19 February); ADWEEK questions whom the Super Bowl ad reached (n0995). Relation to earlier notes: Bitcoin led on 8 and 14 February, was a smaller item on 4 and 9 February, and on 18 February ran as 'digital gold fails the war test' (gold up, BTC down); the earlier draft of this item repeated that digital-gold angle almost verbatim, so it was re-angled to dip-buying faith versus crypto winter and the untraded US proxies (MARA, COIN), with all-new 18-19 February evidence.

Tesla: a new narrative for the month, retail loyalty to a founder in a fight with the SEC (Reuters n0736, Forbes n1851) and a returning short-seller despite low short interest (Teslarati n1711), against TSLA 856.98 USD, -2.21% on 18 February and -9.21% over 20 sessions; breaks on the 416,000-vehicle braking probe (Reuters n1867) and Time's warning that the scandals could hit the bottom line (n1834). Tesla was not an item in earlier retail notes. The NPR Boombox recall (n1866) was removed: that recall was announced on 10 February, outside the seven-day company-news window despite its 17 February index stamp.

GDX: brief carryover, secondary and at most 160 words. Gold miners ran on 14 February ('the invasion hedge with leverage') and GLD on 17 February; this item is kept short and cites only newly published weekend evidence (BBC n1424, Reuters n1422, Axios n1435 on the Belarus extension, Yahoo Finance's GLD trade list n0834), with gold 1,899.80 USD/oz (+3.13% 5s) and GDX +6.38% 5s. The Guardian's Macron summit item (n1430) was removed because the summit-in-principle announcement it reports may post-date 00:00 UTC on 21 February.
considered_not_chosen: ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK -4.96% on 18 February, -9.87% 5s; Cathie Wood n1741, n1757; Bloomberg n1720): new statements, but the narrative repeats the 1 February smaller item and Wood's 'way undervalued' line already appeared in the 18 February Smart Money View.

DraftKings (DKNG -21.62% on 18 February, -25.89% 5s): largest 1-session drop on the card, but no own-date headline on its results beyond a generic sports-betting-margins piece (n1119), so no supportable catalyst or attention evidence.
Upstart (UPST +30.02% 5s, -6.86% 1s): big post-results swing but only a generic 'is now a good time to scoop up' piece (n0576).
Roku (WSJ n0918, Reuters n0793 on a 20% fall): a post-results growth miss close to the 17 and 18 February growth-repricing leads, and no card row.
Defense stocks (ITA -0.84% 5s, LMT -2.46% 5s): no war-trade rally on the card yet.

Recycled 17-18 February attention items not reused: Munger's 'speculative mess' (n1721), Saluzzi's retail rebellion (n1737), the Forbes screenshot (n1722), Newsweek's Twitter look-alike (n1723), Time (n0403) and the Avis meme-stock headline (n1713, a weak mechanical analog).

Avoided as possibly after the cutoff or misdated: n1427, n1440 and n1430 (the Biden-Putin summit 'in principle', announced around or after 00:00 UTC 21 February), n1319 (CNN 'Photos: Russia invades Ukraine', stamped 14 February, misdated), n1866 (NPR Boombox recall, a 10 February event), Reuters LIVE MARKETS blogs (n1274, n1264, n1229, n1218).
